q: What is the unit of ingestion — the thing that gets processed as one indivisible input?
a: A single typed message carrying its own reference time.

q: When the extractor interprets a unit, what surrounding material is it entitled to see?
a: The previous four messages, providing two complete conversation turns.

q: Who is a legitimate subject of memory?
a: Everyone: always the speaker first, plus other significant entities, concepts, or actors mentioned.

q: After extraction, is the raw input kept?
a: Yes, permanently in a non-lossy episode subgraph with source-tracing indices.

q: When does extraction run relative to the interaction?
a: At ingestion, inline; whether it blocks the response is unspecified.

q: What shape must a memory take to be storable?
a: A typed binary relation between two distinct entity nodes; multi-entity facts become repeated pairs.

q: What does an entity carry besides its name?
a: An LLM-generated free-text summary regenerated whenever duplicate entities merge.

q: Is the epistemic status of a stored item represented at all?
a: No; all semantic items are facts without confidence, evidence count, or source type.

q: How is time represented?
a: Bi-temporally, with created and expired transaction times plus valid and invalid event times.

q: Is the relation vocabulary closed?
a: No; the LLM generates relation types ad hoc for each fact.

q: Is there a level of abstraction above individual entities?
a: Yes; dynamically maintained community nodes carry high-level summaries of strongly connected entity clusters.

q: When are two mentions the same thing, and when is that decided?
a: At write time, using hybrid candidate search and LLM resolution, then merging duplicate names and summaries.

q: What must never be stored, regardless of relevance?
a: Nothing; there are no content-based exclusions, sensitive categories, or privacy constraints.

q: What happens to candidates the extractor considered and rejected?
a: They vanish; no drop log exists, while a reflexion pass increases extraction coverage.

q: When new information contradicts stored information, what determines which survives?
a: Recency always wins; the new edge’s valid time becomes the old edge’s invalid time.

q: How wide a net does contradiction-detection cast?
a: Only semantically related existing edges between the same entity pair.

q: Is an invalidated item deleted or retained?
a: Retained with an invalid timestamp to preserve relationship history.

q: May the system decline to resolve a contradiction?
a: No; every detected contradiction is immediately resolved in favor of the newer edge.

q: What does the retriever return when nothing relevant exists?
a: The top k results anyway, without a threshold, null return, or relevance floor.

q: How are candidates found?
a: Through hybrid embedding cosine search, BM25 full-text search, and breadth-first graph traversal.

q: What determines rank among retrieved candidates?
a: A configurable reranker: RRF, MMR, node distance, cross-encoder score, or episode-mention frequency.

q: What does memory hand to the generator?
a: A flat text string containing facts with date ranges and entities with summaries.

q: How much context is returned?
a: A fixed top-k context, averaging about 1,600 tokens, regardless of query.

q: Are retrieval and disclosure separable?
a: No; retrieved content enters the context string and is available to the answer.

q: Is provenance available to whoever consumes the memory?
a: Structurally yes through episode-entity indices, but it is absent from the generator context.

q: Who can correct the memory?
a: No one directly; correction only occurs when later conversation contradicts stored information.

q: What does the system do when it doesn't know?
a: Nothing special; it has no abstention path, confidence output, or unanswerable-question handling.

q: Does anything lose standing without being contradicted?
a: No; facts remain current until contradicted, with no decay, expiry, last-seen field, or confirmation event.

q: How does the aggregate layer stay current, and what is drift worth?
a: Single-step label propagation updates it on insert, with periodic full community refreshes to correct drift.

q: Which model constructs the graph?
a: GPT-4o-mini constructs the graph throughout.
